findings.description: The user_data script exports a static AWS access key ID and secret access key in cleartext. EC2 user data is retrievable via the instance metadata service (including through SSRF from the internet-facing Apache server) and is stored in plaintext in Terraform state, leaking long-lived AWS credentials.
Ingress allows TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access on a publicly addressed instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts.

Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and the user_data provisions Apache serving plain HTTP with no TLS listener, so traffic to and from the host is transmitted in cleartext and subject to interception or tampering.

Egress permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing no outbound boundary and easing data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised host that also holds hard-coded AWS credentials.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true (the attribute is explicitly commented out), so data on the attached volume is stored unencrypted at rest.
The snapshot is derived from an unencrypted EBS volume and therefore inherits no encryption, so snapshot data can be copied, shared, or restored without cryptographic protection.
The VPC flow log bucket declares no server-side encryption configuration, leaving sensitive network telemetry stored without an explicitly enforced encryption key.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or restrictive bucket policy is defined for the flow log bucket, so an ACL or policy change could expose network telemetry publicly; there is also no policy requiring aws:SecureTransport for access.

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains available; on an internet-facing web server this allows SSRF to read instance metadata and user_data, which contains hard-coded AWS credentials.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so unless the AMI snapshot is encrypted the root volume is created unencrypted and any data written to it is stored in cleartext.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true combined with the route table's 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway places the web host directly on the public internet with no load balancer or NAT boundary.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true and association with the internet-gateway route table make every instance launched in this subnet publicly reachable by default.
